purpose: Improve cyclic federated XGBoost by enhancing components separately (base learner, then cyclic federation), then recombine and test once on development data
history: Cyclic XGBoost v1 (2 passes x 5 rounds) and v2 (10 passes x 1 round) were screened and scrapped on development data; v2 mean 0.6244 vs block128 0.6219 but failed at seed 27 by 0.1 pt; DoS recall ~49% vs 72%. This study is development-adaptive in motivation, so selection is moved off the development rows.
tuning_split: Fit rows with sha256('tradecraft-xgb-tuning-v1:' || int64 row id) first byte < 51 (~20%) form the tuning holdout; the rest is tuning-train. Each client keeps its own tuning-train rows. Development rows are not used in stages 1-2.
tuning_metric: Macro-F1 on the tuning holdout at a 5% benign false-alert threshold calibrated on the holdout's own benign rows (selection metric only; slightly optimistic and identical for all variants). Per-class recall, DoS recall and serialized model bytes are reported.

stage1_central.selection: One-at-a-time variants first. Then at most three predeclared-style combinations of improving variants (chosen after stage-1a, still on the tuning holdout). Prefer the smaller serialized model when tuning macro-F1 is within 0.005.

stage1b_amendment.recorded_after: stage-1a holdout results: base 0.6983 (3.91 MB); rounds400 0.6994 (8.11 MB); multi_output_tree 0.6882 (1.72 MB); balanced weights 0.6549 with DoS 0.901, Web 0.439, Brute 0.409; others <= base

power0.75.why: between sqrt and balanced; DoS is the class lost in cyclic federation

mot_rounds400.why: recover multi_output_tree quality at < base size

stage1b_amendment.stage2_inputs: Carry forward the best tuning-F1 configuration and the smallest configuration within 0.01 of it (cost candidate)
stage1b_amendment.stage2_inputs_resolved: rounds400 is best (0.6994) but ~2x base model size, so its cyclic payload (~115 MB) cannot meet the 88 MB stage-3 ceiling; it is replaced by base (0.6983, within 0.0011). Cost candidate: mot_rounds400 (0.6952, 3.46 MB). Also carried: power0.75, because DoS recall is the observed cyclic failure and it is the strongest DoS lever with tuning F1 within 0.013 of best. Recorded before any stage-2 run.

stage2_cyclic.base_scheme: v2: 10 passes x 1 boosting round per visit, per-pass permutation default_rng(SeedSequence([seed, pass, 777]))

variants.eta_decay: eta per pass = stage-1 eta x cosine factor from 1.0 to 0.3 across passes
variants.size_weighted: Each pass visits clients in proportion to tuning-train size (same 200 total visits), order shuffled per pass

stage2_cyclic.selection: Highest mean tuning macro-F1 across seeds 7 and 17; ties prefer lower payload

stage3_final.train: Selected configuration and scheme on all fit rows of each client (no holdout), seeds 7/17/27
stage3_final.evaluation: Development audit at the frozen alarm split, once
stage3_final.rule: Unchanged from v1/v2: at EVERY seed macro-F1 >= same-seed block128 - 0.01, absolute actual FAR difference <= 0.005, payload <= 88,058,880 bytes; additionally mean macro-F1 >= block128 mean. Class drops > 0.10 vs block128 flagged.

payload: Serialized UBJSON: each visit uploads its new trees; every tree downloaded once by each of the other 19 clients
process_isolation: Training imports numpy and xgboost only; scoring runs in a separate torch process
limitations: One client partition; development rows previously examined in v1/v2; global class weights. Exploratory only.
